claims.claim: Facebook announced the News Feed feature on September 6, 2006; before then users had to visit individual profiles to see new posts.
claims.episode_span: In September 2006, Facebook rolled out its News Feed feature to give every user a personalized stream of updates rather than forcing them to hunt across separate profile pages.
claims.supporting_quote: On September 6, 2006, Facebook announced a new home page feature called "News Feed"

claims.claim: Facebook passed 100 million registered users in 2008 and 500 million in July 2010.
claims.episode_span: monthly active users rose from roughly 100 million in 2008 to more than 500 million by 2010
claims.supporting_quote: Facebook passed 100 million registered users in 2008, [ 138 ] and 500 million in July 2010. [ 139 ] According to the company's data at the July 2010 announcement, half of the site's membership used Facebook daily

claims.claim: For roughly three years Facebook's algorithms scored posts receiving emoji reactions, including the 'angry' reaction, five times higher than likes, and internal researchers later found posts with 'angry' reactions were much more likely to be toxic, polarizing, fake or low quality.
claims.episode_span: Internal documents later reviewed by researchers showed that posts expressing outrage traveled farther and faster through the network than comparable neutral content.
claims.supporting_quote: The Washington Post reported that for three years, Facebook's algorithms promoted posts receiving the new reactions (including the 'angry' reaction) from its users; giving them a score five times that of traditional likes. Years later, Facebook's researchers pointed out that posts with 'angry' reactions were much more likely to be toxic, polarizing, fake or low quality.

claims.claim: In 2021 whistleblower Frances Haugen released internal Facebook documents showing the company was aware of harmful societal effects from its platforms, leading to The Wall Street Journal's Facebook Files reporting.
claims.episode_span: After the 2021 release of internal research and whistleblower testimony, Facebook announced adjustments to its ranking systems
claims.supporting_quote: In 2021, an internal document leak from Facebook (now Meta Platforms , or Meta) showed it was aware of harmful societal effects from its platforms, yet persisted in prioritizing profit over addressing these harms. The leak, released by whistleblower Frances Haugen , resulted in reporting from The Wall Street Journal in September

claims.claim: In 2018 Facebook overhauled its News Feed algorithm to favor 'Meaningful Social Interactions' (MSI), which increased the weight of reshared material.
claims.episode_span: Subsequent attempts to introduce "meaningful social interaction" signals or down-rank certain categories of content produced mixed results
claims.supporting_quote: In 2018, Facebook overhauled its News Feed algorithm, implementing a new algorithm which favored "Meaningful Social Interactions" or "MSI". The new algorithm increased the weight of reshared material

claims.claim: Facebook did not reduce the ranking weight of the 'angry' reaction until September 2019, when its value was cut to zero.
claims.episode_span: Facebook announced adjustments to its ranking systems aimed at reducing the distribution of content that incited anger
claims.supporting_quote: the company did not differentiate the 'angry' reaction from other reactions until September 2019, when its value was cut to zero
